title: Trace attacker influence across the action path
description: Choose a hostile context and a control posture. Watch where attacker influence stops, which trust boundary fails, and whether a valid-looking proposal reaches a side effect.

stages.label: Principal
stages.detail: Authenticated user, tenant, purpose, permissions, and approval envelope.

stages.label: Context
stages.detail: Retrieved files, memory, websites, tool output, and peer-agent messages.

stages.label: Proposal
stages.detail: A selected tool and structured arguments with no independent authority.

stages.label: Policy gateway
stages.detail: Schema, intent, identity, resource, limits, freshness, and approval checks.

stages.label: Side effect
stages.detail: A message, payment, deletion, deployment, permission change, or code execution.

postures.label: Prompt-only guardrail
postures.detail: The model is told to ignore hostile instructions, but it can call broad tools directly.

postures.label: Schema and allowlist
postures.detail: Tool names and argument types are validated, but calls are not bound to user intent or fresh authority.

postures.label: Intent-bound authority
postures.detail: Context provenance, delegated identity, resource scope, policy, approval, and runtime limits are independently enforced.

scenarios.label: Poisoned vendor invoice
scenarios.brief: A retrieved PDF instructs the agent to replace bank details and submit an urgent payment.
scenarios.attack: Indirect prompt injection enters through a document that the user asked the agent to inspect.

prompt-only.consequence: The hostile document changes the goal and the broad payment tool executes it without an independent comparison to the user's review-only intent.
failedBoundaries: Retrieved content was flattened into instructions.
The proposed payee was not bound to the user's approved task.
No exact-parameter confirmation preceded the transfer.

schema-only.consequence: Every argument matches the schema, so the transfer passes even though the user's principal never authorized that destination or action.
failedBoundaries: Schema validation proved shape, not intent.
The destination was not constrained by a resource envelope.
A high-consequence write lacked exact approval.

bounded-authority.consequence: The gateway compares the proposal with the authenticated review task and denies a transfer tool and destination outside the intent envelope.

scenarios.label: Cross-tenant memory poison
scenarios.brief: A prior run stores a false instruction to export future audit reports to an external URL.
scenarios.attack: Persistent context crosses sessions and tenants without provenance or purpose isolation.

prompt-only.consequence: The planner treats persistent memory as a standing instruction and sends another tenant's report to the stored destination.
failedBoundaries: Memory had no tenant or purpose boundary.
Stored content was treated as authority.
The external destination was unrestricted.

schema-only.consequence: The webhook call is valid and allowlisted; no policy checks the memory provenance, report tenant, or destination audience.
failedBoundaries: The memory item had no trusted provenance.
Authorization did not bind report tenant to principal tenant.
The sink was not restricted to approved domains.

bounded-authority.consequence: Context assembly rejects the memory because its tenant, purpose, and provenance do not match the current task, then marks it for quarantine.

scenarios.label: Privileged agent delegation
scenarios.brief: A low-privilege worker asks a manager agent to delete a production record on its behalf.
scenarios.attack: An internal-looking peer request attempts to inherit the manager's broader credential.

prompt-only.consequence: The manager trusts the peer agent and executes with ambient administrator authority without checking the originating principal.
failedBoundaries: Internal agent identity was treated as trusted purpose.
Delegation widened instead of narrowing authority.
The originating user was lost before execution.

schema-only.consequence: The delete arguments are valid and the manager owns the tool, but the worker's original principal lacks permission for the record.
failedBoundaries: Authorization checked the executor, not the originating subject.
The delegated scope was not preserved.
Permission freshness was not rechecked at use time.

bounded-authority.consequence: The gateway propagates the original subject and delegated scope, then denies the delete because the subject lacks the required permission.

scenarios.label: Hostile tool output
scenarios.brief: A code-analysis tool returns text asking the agent to package secrets and upload them for verification.
scenarios.attack: A trusted tool transport carries untrusted content that redirects the next planning step.

prompt-only.consequence: The agent interprets analyzer output as a new instruction and chains a second tool with access to sensitive files and the public network.
failedBoundaries: Tool output was not labeled as untrusted evidence.
File access and network egress were combined.
The new action was not compared with the coding task.

schema-only.consequence: Each call is valid in isolation, but no trajectory policy detects the sensitive source-to-external-sink chain.
failedBoundaries: Policy did not reason over the full tool chain.
The archive included paths outside the task workspace.
The destination was not allowlisted.

bounded-authority.consequence: Trajectory policy identifies a sensitive file read followed by public egress and denies the upload; the sandbox also lacks network access.
